land.text: the Slavs who revolted 'in 623-24', 'assumed originally subject to Avar rulers (kagans)'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Avar shape of 617-622 overlaps about 52,000 km2 of Samo's 623 shape (the Alpine Slav lands); the Avars' dominance over the Slavs 'came to an end' in 626 after Constantinople (Carantania page).

land.text: 'A smaller part of the original March of the Slavs, centred north of modern Klagenfurt, preserved independence'

successors.note: Carantania's infobox lists Samo's Empire as its predecessor; Cliopatria's Carantania row starts 661.

land.text: 'the Avars returned to their earlier territories, at least southernmost modern Slovakia'

successors.note: Only the southernmost Slovakia is named by the page.

rulers.name: Samo
rulers.note: A Frankish merchant who 'went to the Slavs in c. 623-624' (Fredegar); king 'during a revolt of 623-24' or after the Avar defeat of 626; died 658 or 659 (the page: 'Death of King Samo', infobox 631-658).

keyframe_review.note: 188,500 km2 (bbox 12.1-20.5E, 45.5-51.2N): Bohemia (about 59,000 km2), Moravia and Lower Austria, the Silesian slice, western Slovakia and an Alpine part of about 40,000 km2 that Cliopatria later gives to Carantania. The page: 'It is generally believed that the tribal union included the regions of Moravia, Nitravia (Nitra), Silesia, Bohemia and Lusatia'; archaeology puts it 'in present-day Moravia, Lower Austria and Slovakia'; 'The extent of Samo's power before and after 631 is disputed'. The Alpine part rests on one source (J. B. Bury, quoted on the page: the assumption that the kingdom embraced Carantania 'rests only upon' it). The page gives no area; the frontier is soft.

correction.text: shape unchanged; it holds 627-630, not to 632

keyframe_review.note: 189,438 km2: the 623 shape plus 506 km2 on the southern edge (drawing noise). It holds 627-630 and no longer to 632, because the Dervan Sorbs join in 631 (see the _633 verdict). The Carantania page: 626 'brought an end to Avar dominance over Slavs'.

correction.text: shape unchanged; it holds 631-637, from the Sorbs' accession after Wogastisburg

keyframe_review.note: 210,987 km2: the 627 shape plus about 23,500 km2 along the west and north (bbox to 51.7N and 12.1E): the Sorbs of Lusatia. The Sorbs page: the Surbi under Dervan 'joined the Slavic tribal union of Samo, after Samo's decisive victory against Frankish King Dagobert I in 631' (the Samo and Wogastisburg pages say 631 or 632); it holds from 631, not 633. The Elbe-Saale line marks the limit of Slavic migration west (page).
211,380 km2: the 633 shape plus 506 km2 (noise); no event on the page in 638-640.

211,315 km2, unchanged: 'In 641, the rebellious Radulf sought an alliance with Samo against his sovereign, Sigebert III', which moves no border. The Duchy of Thuringia lies at 9.2-12.3E, west of the shape.

correction.text: shape unchanged; it holds 656-658, not to 660

keyframe_review.note: 211,315 km2, unchanged to 660 in Cliopatria. Samo died in 658 or 659 and 'The history of the tribal union after Samo's death in 658 or 659 is largely unclear ... though it is generally assumed that it ended'; the infobox dates the realm 631-658. The shape holds 656-658.

region.text: the Slavs of Bohemia, Moravia and the Danube lands who revolted in 623-24

ledger.note: c. 623: the Frankish merchant Samo becomes the Slavs' king in their revolt against the Avars. 'According to Fredegar, Samo, a Frankish merchant, went to the Slavs in c. 623-624'; he became king 'during a revolt of 623-24' (or, the page allows, after the Avar defeat of 626). The page gives no capital and no boundary; the shape is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Sorbs' land in Lusatia (and a strip along the western edge): the Surbi under Dervan 'joined the Slavic tribal union of Samo'

ledger.note: 631: after Wogastisburg Dervan's Sorbs join Samo. 'they joined the Slavic tribal union of Samo, after Samo's decisive victory against Frankish King Dagobert I in 631'. The Samo page: Dervan joined 'after Samo defeated Dagobert I'. The Sorbs settled 'by the Elbe, Saale, Spree, and Neisse'. The region is Cliopatria's 633 addition (23,500 km2), which also has a strip the pages do not explain; the dux Dervan is dated 'fl. 615-636' (Dervan page).

region.text: 'A smaller part of the original March of the Slavs, centred north of modern Klagenfurt'

ledger.note: 658: Samo dies and the tribal union breaks up; the Alpine Slavs keep their independence. 'In 658 Samo died and his Tribal Union disintegrated. A smaller part of the original March of the Slavs, centred north of modern Klagenfurt, preserved independence.' Cliopatria's Carantania row starts 661.

658: the Avars return to the south of the former realm. 'After Samo's death, the Avars returned to their earlier territories, at least southernmost modern Slovakia.' The page names only the south; the whole Slovak part of the shape is the researcher's cautious upper bound and the rest of Slovakia is left to the next event.

region.text: Bohemia, Moravia, Lusatia, Silesia and the Danube lands, whose later history 'is largely unclear'

ledger.note: 658: the realm's core falls apart into tribes. 'The history of the tribal union after Samo's death in 658 or 659 is largely unclear ... though it is generally assumed that it ended.' The Sorbs page also gives 658 and calls the tribes' fate 'undetermined'. Confidence 1: the land going to no state is the reading of a silence.
658: the end of Samo's union. Infobox 631-658; 'Death of King Samo'; the page allows 658 or 659 and Cliopatria keeps the row to 660.

wars.name: Slavic revolt against the Avars
wars.outcome: The page has Samo become king 'during a revolt of 623-24' or after the Avar defeat of 626; the Carantania page says 626 'brought an end to Avar dominance over Slavs, as the Avars were defeated at Constantinople'.
wars.note: No battle against the Avars is dated on the pages opened.

wars.name: Battle of Wogastisburg
wars.outcome: Dagobert I led three armies of 'Alamanni, Lombards, and Austrasian Franks'; 'the main fighting force was defeated in a three-day siege' (Slavic victory, 'Enlargement of Samo's realm'). Valuk, 'duke of the Wends', 'allowed Longobards to pass through his territory and attack Samo from south-west' (Samo page, c. 630-631).
wars.note: The battle's place is unknown ('There is no conclusive evidence for any of these locations'): Rubín, Úhošť, Bratislava, Trenčín, Beckov, Vienna and others. 631 or 632 on both pages.

wars.name: Samo's raids on Thuringia
wars.outcome: Samo 'raided Frankish Thuringia several times after the battle'; Dervan fought Thuringia 631-634 and was defeated by Radulf in 636; 'In 641, the rebellious Radulf sought an alliance with Samo against his sovereign, Sigebert III'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Sorbs page says only that the Slavic tribes 'continuously raided Thuringia'.

certainty.note: The page: 'The extent of Samo's power before and after 631 is disputed'; no capital, no treaty line, no survey. The Alpine part (Carantania) and the Silesian and Lusatian edges are the softest; the Elbe-Saale line is the Slavic limit in the west.

notes: Samo's Empire, eu-15-a. The Samo's Empire page gives no capital and no area; Wogastisburg is unlocated, so identity.capitals is empty. Cliopatria's shape includes about 40,000 km2 of Alpine Slav land that its later Carantania row takes; J. B. Bury (quoted on the page) says the inclusion of Carantania 'rests only upon' one source, the Carantania page lists Samo's Empire as its predecessor. Kept, flagged soft. The 633 enlargement is dated 631 by the Sorbs page (Samo and Wogastisburg pages: 631 or 632); the verdicts re-date the Cliopatria shapes by verdict (shape unchanged). End 658 follows the infobox; Cliopatria runs to 660. After 658 the pages say the union 'is largely unclear'; the land is given to Carantania (the Alpine part), the Avars (southern Slovakia) and nobody (the rest). The Dervan page opened was a disambiguation list and added only 'fl. 615-636, Sorbian medieval ruler'; the Sorbs page was used for Dervan. Counterpart 'Sorbs under Dervan' has no Cliopatria row. Fredegar, the main source, was not opened (not a Wikipedia page within the budget). The Kingdom of the Franks and Duchy of Thuringia dossiers belong to eu-07 and eu-06.
